titulo: First stdio server with the official SDK, tested in the Inspector
lead: The simplest way to connect a service to an agent is stdio: the client starts your program and talks to it over stdin and stdout. In this lesson you install the kit with pinned versions, read the class server, and call the tool two ways: with a test client and with the MCP Inspector in command-line mode.
objetivo: start an MCP server over stdio with the official v2 SDK and call it with a test client and with the Inspector, no host at all.

aprende.t: Install the kit with npm ci and check the versions
The createServer factory and the SDK v2 serveStdio
Call the tool through Inspector 2.11.0 in --cli mode
Why every log goes to stderr

hero_alt: Unbranded mini computer with a lit white LED, connected by cable to a blurred laptop showing a terminal.

secoes.titulo: From npm ci to the first call

nos.detalhe: The kit's package-lock.json pins the versions: @modelcontextprotocol/server and client 2.3.1, node 2.1.1, ext-apps 2.0.3, zod 4.6.7. npm ci installs exactly those.
A function that builds an McpServer and registers tools, a resource, and a prompt. The SDK calls the factory when it needs an instance.
serveStdio(createServer) reads requests from stdin and writes responses to stdout. The process waits until a client speaks.
Whoever starts the process. In the kit: teste-stdio.mjs (an SDK client) and the MCP Inspector in --cli mode. Later, Claude Code and Codex play the same role (lesson 8).

secoes.sub: Once. You need Node 20 or newer and git. The blocks in the next lessons start from this folder.

blocos.conteudo:
git clone https://github.com/inematds/formacao-webmcp-mcp-v72 ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-mcp-v72
cd ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-mcp-v72/kit
npm ci                      # installs the versions from package-lock.json
npm ls --depth=0

secoes.titulo: Call it through the test client
secoes.sub: The test plays the role of Claude Code: it starts node stdio.mjs, negotiates the revision, and calls buscar_turmas.

blocos.conteudo:
cd "$(mktemp -d)" && cp ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-mcp-v72/kit/*.mjs ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-mcp-v72/kit/package.json .
node teste-stdio.mjs 2>&1 | grep -m1 -o "ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND\|Cannot find package '[^']*'"; echo "saída: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

abas.html:
turmas: servidor MCP no stdio
era: modern · ferramentas: buscar_turmas, reservar_vaga
buscar_turmas → 2 turmas
saída: 0

The first line came from the server's stderr; the rest came from the client.

abas.rot: Common error: you forgot npm ci
abas.html:
ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND
saída: 1

Captured with the "common error" block above, which copies the files to an empty folder, without node_modules. Fix: run npm ci inside kit/.

secoes.titulo: Call it through the MCP Inspector, without opening a browser
secoes.sub: Inspector 2.11.0 has a command-line mode. The version is pinned in npx so the result matches the capture.

blocos.conteudo:
cd ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-mcp-v72/kit
npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@2.11.0 --cli node stdio.mjs \
  --method tools/call --tool-name buscar_turmas --tool-arg termo=html
echo "saída: $?"

abas.html:
turmas: servidor MCP no stdio
{
  "content": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": "html-01 · HTML semântico para agentes · 3 vagas"
    }
  ],
  "structuredContent": {
    "turmas": [
      {
        "id": "html-01",
        "titulo": "HTML semântico para agentes",
        "vagas": 3
      }
    ]
  }
}
saída: 0

Without --cli, the same command opens the Inspector web interface, where you connect and test the tools by clicking.

paragrafos: On stdio, every line of stdout is read as a JSON-RPC message. That's why the kit logs with console.error (stderr). The SDK documentation warns that a console.log corrupts the channel and the host may drop the connection.
In our test on 10/19/2026, the SDK 2.3.1 client and Inspector 2.11.0 skipped a stray line and kept going. Don't count on that: another host may not be so forgiving. Always log to stderr.

Prefer Python? The official mcp 2.3.0 SDK (PyPI) also ships the 2026-07-28 revision (server/discover and InputRequiredResult in the package code). This course stays in Node; the concepts apply the same way.

secoes.sub: Rehearsal on the kit and one change of your own.

exercicios.pronto: node teste-stdio.mjs → era: modern · ferramentas: buscar_turmas, reservar_vaga and saída: 0; the Inspector returns a JSON with "structuredContent".

exercicios.titulo: E5 · A class of your own
exercicios.texto: Add a class to TURMAS in servidor.mjs with the word mcp in the title and run the test again.

perguntas.p: On the stdio transport, who starts the server process?
opcoes: The server itself, as a system service
The client, which talks over stdin and stdout
The Inspector, always, even in Claude Code
perguntas.explica: On stdio, the client (Claude Code, Codex, Inspector, the kit's test) starts the process and owns its lifetime.

perguntas.p: Why does the kit use npm ci instead of npm install?
opcoes: It installs exactly the versions in package-lock.json
It's faster in every case, with no other practical difference
It always downloads the newest published version of the official SDK
perguntas.explica: The course was tested with 2.3.1; npm ci guarantees those versions. npm install may move up to a version that behaves differently.

perguntas.p: Where should the stdio server write its logs?
perguntas.explica: stdout is the protocol channel. Even if one client tolerates a stray line, another may drop the connection.

perguntas.p: The test shows era: modern. What does that guarantee?
opcoes: That the server only accepts new clients and refuses old ones
That client and server agreed on the 2026-07-28 revision
That Node is on the newest version
That the server now responds over the SSE transport
perguntas.explica: The client asked for mode: 'auto' and the server offered 2026-07-28. An older client is still served by the same server (lesson 4).

itens.texto: npm ci with the kit's lock: SDK v2 2.3.1.
One createServer factory; serveStdio is the door.
SDK client and Inspector --cli, no host and no cost.
